QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_7

answer.text: The fraction of outcome attributable to partners or co-implementers
The fraction of outcome produced at the expense of another group (negative externality)
The fraction of outcome that fades away over time post-intervention
The fraction of outcome that would have occurred even without the SE's intervention

explanation.text: The Logic: Deadweight is the counterfactual baseline — the amount of outcome that would have occurred anyway without the SE's intervention. It is deducted from gross outcome to isolate the SE's net contribution in the SROI calculation. The Trap: Option 2 is DISPLACEMENT. Option 3 is DROP-OFF. Option 4 is ATTRIBUTION. All four are SROI adjustments but target different distortions. Cross-Exam Context: IMP CONTRIBUTION dimension captures the same concept by asking 'what would likely occur anyway?' — XXIII expects the assessor to know both the IMP label and the SROI label. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Evidence deadweight via control-group comparison, secular trend data (e.g., state-level literacy improvement) or published RCT results on similar interventions — never rely on SE-supplied deadweight estimates without independent triangulation.
